headers.//: The rule above matches on the REQUEST path, and nobody ever requests index.html by name — the kiosk asks for /kiosk-app/ and the rewrite resolves it to index.html internally. So the app shell fell through to Firebase's default max-age=3600 and browsers held a stale copy for an hour. That is how a kiosk ended up still running a pre-deploy bundle after a deploy: the agent was healthy, the URL was right, and the page simply was not the one we had shipped. Matching the shell paths themselves is what actually applies. Hashed assets under assets/ keep their own long cache, so this costs one revalidation per load, not a re-download.

Content Security Policy. The pages are served from here, not from Express, so this is where it has to live. script-src is 'self' with no unsafe-inline and no unsafe-eval: the build emits one external module and no inline script, so nothing legitimate needs them — and that is what stops an injected <script> from running at all. style-src keeps unsafe-inline because the component library sets style attributes directly on elements; style injection is a far smaller problem than script injection. connect-src names the API and its WebSocket explicitly, so even injected code has nowhere to send anything. frame-src allows the Google viewer used for Office previews and blob: for the generated booklet PDF. frame-ancestors 'none' is the clickjacking defence for the admin pages.

headers.value: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com; font-src 'self' data: https://fonts.gstatic.com; img-src 'self' data: blob:; connect-src 'self' https://140.245.224.137.nip.io wss://140.245.224.137.nip.io; frame-src 'self' blob: https://docs.google.com; worker-src 'self' blob:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; upgrade-insecure-requests
